summary: Uvira territory is the southern front between AFC/M23 and the government camp in Sud-Kivu. After taking Bukavu and Kamanyola in February 2025, M23 held the northern Ruzizi plain while Wazalendo (Bafuliiru/Babembe Mai-Mai), FARDC and Burundian FDNB troops held Uvira city, where Wazalendo frequently overrode FARDC command. In a December 2025 offensive M23 swept down the plain (Luvungi, Sange, Kiliba) and entered Uvira around 10 December 2025, then announced and carried out a withdrawal from the city under US pressure in December 2025–January 2026, after which Wazalendo and returning state forces re-occupied it. As of the reference date the city and southern plain are assessed as Wazalendo-dominated but contested and fragile, the northern plain toward Kamanyola as M23-held, the Bafuliiru mid-plateaux (Lemera, Langala, Ndolera) as Wazalendo/Mai-Mai areas and the Banyamulenge high plateaux (Mulenge, Rubuga/Kitoga) as Twirwaneho areas allied to M23. Confidence is low throughout. Live web research was impossible for this unit (search budget exhausted, news/UN sites blocked by the egress proxy); assessment rests on background knowledge up to mid-2026 and should be re-checked. Review (2026-10-01): the reviewer could not run independent web research either (search budget exhausted; Wikipedia, ReliefWeb, Actualite.cd and Bing blocked by the egress proxy), so zones were checked only for internal and geographic consistency against neighbouring Walungu and Fizi assessments; no controller changes were made and all zones remain low confidence.

sources.title: Reuters Africa coverage of the M23 capture of Uvira (Dec 2025) and announced withdrawal
Kivu Security Tracker (Uvira territory armed groups: Mai-Mai/Wazalendo, Twirwaneho, RED-Tabara)

zones.description: Uvira city (all neighbourhoods/health areas of Uvira HZ) and contiguous lakeshore settlements Kagando, Kahorohoro, Kabimba, Katoso
zones.evidence: In 2025 Wazalendo groups were the dominant armed presence in Uvira, imposing city shutdowns and blocking FARDC appointments; M23 entered the city around 10 December 2025 and then withdrew under US pressure in December 2025–January 2026, after which Wazalendo re-entered and state forces partially redeployed. Control after the withdrawal, and whether M23 has returned, could not be verified for the reference date.

zones.description: Southern Ruzizi plain just north of Uvira: Kiliba (Musenga, Kitona/Kagando HA), Hongero/Kahwizi, Runingu/Kagurube, Biriba, Kasambura
zones.evidence: The Kiliba–Runingu stretch lay on M23's December 2025 advance route to Uvira and became a buffer/front area after the announced M23 pull-back; Wazalendo and FARDC are assessed to hold it with M23 positions to the north. Exact frontline position as of the reference date is not verified.

zones.description: Northern Ruzizi plain toward Kamanyola: Sange (Maendeleo), Luvungi/Mirungu (Mayengo), Katogota (Cepac), Lubarika (Rutora), Luberizi (Mission), Bwegera, Mutarule, Nyakabere, Ndunda, Rusabagi, Kimuka, Kigurwe
zones.evidence: M23 held Kamanyola and the Katogota–Luvungi edge of the plain from February 2025 and overran Luvungi, Luberizi and Sange in early December 2025; its withdrawal pledge concerned Uvira city, and it is assessed to have kept the northern plain with Wazalendo incursions.

zones.description: Bafuliiru mid-plateaux (Lemera, Langala/Rubenga, Ndolera, Kibungu, Buheba, Busulira, Nyamutiri, Kiringye, Mubere/Kiziba) and western hills above the plain (Mugaja/Kala, Mangwa/Kalimba, Luhito/Ruvumera)
zones.evidence: The Moyens Plateaux of Uvira are long-standing bases of Bafuliiru Mai-Mai factions now operating as Wazalendo, with Burundian rebels (RED-Tabara) present in the hills; the state has little permanent presence. Possible M23 advances toward Lemera since late 2025 are not verified.

zones.description: North-west hills in Kaziba health zone bordering Walungu (Kashunju/Ntagereka, Kalemba, Burhurhu)
zones.evidence: These localities belong to the Kaziba health zone of Walungu territory, held by M23 since its February 2025 southern advance, with Wazalendo active in the hills toward Lemera.

zones.description: Banyamulenge high plateaux of Uvira: Mulenge, Rubuga (Wimbongo), Kitoga (Ruhuha)
zones.evidence: The Banyamulenge high plateaux are the stronghold of Twirwaneho self-defence groups, which allied with AFC/M23 and pushed FARDC out of Minembwe and surrounding plateaux in 2025; Mai-Mai/Wazalendo contest the lower edges.
